title: on-deploy
description: the doftiles deployment orchestrator: verifies the WM-stack binaries, installs the missing ones through per-distro deploy scripts, runs the make install assurances (bun, postinstall trust, the herbctl binary), deploys the dependencies, and provisions the session stack from declarative profiles.

content.heading: on-deploy - the deployment orchestrator
content: **on-deploy** turns the **doftiles** repo into a one-command deployment. it runs inside the doftiles checkout, reads the deployment manifests, and provisions the session stack from them - all four manifests are configurable through configure (tui or flags).
[https://github.com/akinevz2/on-deploy](https://github.com/akinevz2/on-deploy)

content.heading: the repo it walks
content: the doftiles checkout is a structured deployment scope, declared in four manifests:
**wm.required** - required binaries, the deployment model and the deploy target
**stows.required** - the stow packages
**system.required** - each submodule with its dots-relative paths - the scope of the depends walk
**services.required** - the unit order
each stow package owns its own dots/<pkg>/.local/state/depends/<pkg>.makefile (toolchain/build/link/install), and the session runs as systemd user units - on-deploy provisions both.

content.heading: the package, architecturally
content: a resolver, not a package list: the deploy script contract is `<target>.deploy <binary>` → the providing package, and `install <binary>` → the install command - one resolver script per distro, whatever the distro is.

the requirement walk is resolve, confirm, run, re-verify: every missing binary is resolved per <target>.deploy, printed before it runs (sudo prompts stay visible - the tty is unlocked), and re-verified after.
the prompts ride a raw line reader (bun's readline wedges), and the menu works scripted or interactive.

content.heading: usage - the verbs
content: `install` / `check` - the requirement walk; check reports and exits 1 on missing (--json).

`deploy` - install every missing binary: resolve the package, show the command, confirm (Enter = yes), run it, then re-verify - a binary still missing after its command fails the run. `--yes` for non-interactive runs, `--dry-run` to preview.
`services` - the service.order (services.required) runner: check/start/stop/restart/status over the systemd user units, --no-block, stow-safe disable.
`detect-server` - the reachable-X probe (localhost:0.0 style): `--persist-to-systemd` writes DISPLAY into the manager env, `--persist-to-env` writes an rc.d-includable file.
`toolchain` - the make install assurances: bun through npm when missing, trust of the global bun packages' postinstall scripts, the **herbctl** binary built from the submodule checkout when missing.
`depends` - the per-package walk over system.required: every listed package runs its depends makefile; `--only` narrows, `--build` for sync+build.

`snapshot` - collect a machine's pre-existing config into doftiles' defaults/ (a stow-shaped package) before the first deploy overwrites it - the machine's prior state, versioned in git, restorable with one make target.
`configure` - edit the deploy target and the required-package list from an interactive menu (or `--target`/`--add`/`--remove` flags).

content.heading: usage - the profiles
content: four session models, co-installable where it makes sense:

**wsl-systemd** - no display manager: hlwm runs as the systemd user unit herbst.service, waiting for the Windows-side X server (VcXsrv) to be reachable; provision even checks the Windows partition for VcXsrv and offers a silent install from the SourceForge feed

**nested** - hlwm inside an Xvfb framebuffer, shared over VNC (:5900) and browser noVNC (:6080), with an RDP surface layered on top (xrdp's Xvnc module attaches to the same framebuffer; 3389 stays free for the Windows side)
**xinit** - startx runs ~/.xinitrc; no display manager
**greetd** - greetd + tuigreet own the console (the bare-OS target)

a profile declares units (systemd user units) and env overrides (written to ~/.config/doftiles/env, read by the units via EnvironmentFile). the make deploy tui selects the session model, the features, the units and the env - and writes deploy.profile before stowing anything.

content.heading: quirks
content: non-interactive runs abort cleanly demanding --yes instead of blocking on prompts; a failed install fails the run.
the only true external requirement is passwordless sudo (or an interactive prompt) for platform package installation.
profiles enable additively: activating a second profile never disables the first's units.

content.heading: stable in v1.4.x
content: version probing reads the package manager (dpkg-query, pacman) instead of spawning the binary - GUI programs no longer initialize a display backend on the walk and flash a window mid-deploy.
the managed status reports `installed <version>`, read from the same package-manager query.
the four manifests, configure and the profile walk are the stable surface since 1.4.0.
